title: Cramér–Rao as a named variance bound
dek: Var(θ̃) ≥ 1/I(θ) for unbiased estimators under regularity. Wikipedia bound. Attainment is exponential-family/MLE territory.
story: The Cramér–Rao bound on Wikipedia is an inequality: no unbiased estimator can beat 1/I(θ) in variance, under interchange-of-derivative regularity. It is a bound, not an estimator.
MLEs attain it asymptotically in regular exponential families. Biased estimators (James–Stein, smoothing) can beat the bound for MSE — that is the point of shrinkage plates.
Do not quote CRLB as a confidence interval.
deepTitle: Unbiasedness is the price of admission
deep: If you drop unbiasedness, the bound does not apply (shrinkage).
If regularity fails (boundary, non-differentiable density), the bound need not hold.
Multivariate: covariance matrices ordered by I⁻¹.
TB: an unbiased rare-variant frequency estimator can have huge variance; a Bayes shrinker may have better MSE.

visual.caption: Teaching bars: CRLB as a floor for unbiased variance, versus a shrinkage MSE that is allowed to go under that floor because bias was spent.
